summary: Grant writing, donor analytics, and service delivery are the practical uses; governance capacity is the constraint. No single entity keeps a real-time registry of nonprofit AI adoption - coverage comes from sector research organizations, and this page names the ones that actually publish it.

analysis.body:
Per the Census Bureau, the latest Business Trends and Outlook Survey reading shows 13.7% of firms in Other services, NAICS 81, which includes grantmaking and civic organizations, reported using AI in the last two weeks. The prior period figure was 12.6%. This is the closest official measure for nonprofit heavy service sectors, though it covers a broader NAICS grouping rather than nonprofits alone.

The World of AI catalogues four individually verified nonprofit and open source foundation entries. LMSYS stewards Chatbot Arena, a neutral open evaluation platform for benchmarking model quality. Khan Academy is an end user of AI in education, not a producer. Krita Foundation and Blender Foundation steward creative software tools that AI generated imagery and 3D content increasingly intersect with, but their primary missions predate AI. The page notes the list is small and confirms only organizational structure and nonprofit status, not funding scale, compute access, or governance detail.

The AI Equity Project builds structured learning pathways and intergenerational programs, turning public libraries and community spaces into interactive learning environments where senior citizens and student volunteers explore practical AI tools. It operates as a global network providing standardized technical curricula and training assets to underrepresented communities. Its International AI for Impact Challenge invites engineering candidates to pitch operational algorithms, with top participants securing lab partnerships, academic research access, and intellectual property advisement.

NTEN states that nonprofit technology is marked by inequities within organizations and the sector that must be dismantled, and that users, builders, and funders have a responsibility to ensure equitable use of technology. NTEN also runs professional certificates and scholarships, and celebrates open source apps and tools for nonprofit and advocacy groups. Per Candid, the organization tracks grantmaking trends including funding directed toward AI adoption and technology infrastructure, though the excerpt does not provide specific dollar figures. Per CEP, its AI focused reporting examines how foundations and nonprofits use AI for operations, program delivery, and communications.

A reader deciding whether to deploy should note that official adoption is modest and rising slowly, from 12.6% to 13.7% in the Census series. The catalogued nonprofit AI footprint is thin, with no training compute providers, no standards bodies setting grid or data center specifications, and no open model foundations releasing weights. Equity, accessibility, and governance capacity appear as the recurring constraints, while the source excerpts offer no measured ROI evidence to justify investment.

https://cep.org/.brief: The page from the Center for Effective Philanthropy features an article by Kevin Bolduc, who is identified as vice president of assessment and advisory services. The article’s title asks how one collaborative’s movement-led participatory model makes a difference for grantees. The harvested text does not include any further details or findings.

https://candid.org/.brief: Candid offers grants and nonprofit data intended to help users find funding, research organizations, and connect with funders. According to Candid, a survey of rural community members found trust in local libraries, nonprofits, and community foundations remained high. Candid also notes that three years of Social Impact Staff Retention survey data point to consistent reasons why nonprofit staff stay or leave. Additionally, it states that donor-advised fund donations are the fastest-growing form of giving in the United States and provides a Tableau dashboard to explore where those dollars go. Since the late 1950s, Candid has worked to open public access to philanthropic funding information.

https://www.nten.org/.brief: NTEN presents itself as a nonprofit community focused on using technology for social change. It offers networking opportunities, job listings, and professional development resources such as certificates and scholarships. Members can pledge to use an Equity Guide and support open-source developers. NTEN also encourages participation in committees on accessibility, equity, and programs.

https://theaiequityproject.org/.brief: The AI Equity Project reports that it develops structured educational routes and cross-generational initiatives aimed at making AI usable, ethical, and practical for every community. It says it converts public libraries and local community venues into hands-on learning settings where older adults and student volunteers jointly try out practical AI tools. The organization also describes a worldwide network that supplies standardized technical curricula and training materials to underrepresented groups, with support structures meant to ensure each student directly helps deploy machine learning architectures. Its International AI for Impact Challenge asks engineering candidates to propose operational algorithms for real-world issues, and top entrants receive engineering lab partnerships, academic research access, and intellectual property advice.

https://theworldofai.org/ai-ecosystem/ec.brief: The page catalogs four individually verified nonprofit and open-source organizations, each with a sourced classification note. It states that LMSYS stewards Chatbot Arena, a shared evaluation platform, while Khan Academy is an end-user of AI in education, and the Krita and Blender foundations steward creative software tools that intersect with AI-generated imagery and 3D content. The page notes that none of these are infrastructure builders in the compute-or-power sense, and the list excludes training compute providers, standards bodies, and open-model foundations that release weights. It also says the notes confirm only organizational structure and nonprofit status, not funding scale, compute access, or governance detail.
